plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the StyleGAN architecture, organized into three labeled vertical columns: the main generative pipeline (center), the noise injection branch (left of center), and the style branch (right). In the style branch, a latent variable z (1×1×512) is passed through a fully connected network to produce an intermediate variable w (1×1×512), which then feeds three separate linear transforms (each outputting 2×1×512) to generate style vectors y₁, y₂, y₃ that apply per-channel scale and offset adjustments at successive resolution levels of the generator. The main generative pipeline begins with a learned constant input (4×4×512) and passes through convolutional blocks that double in spatial resolution from 4×4×512 to 8×8×512, with each block receiving the corresponding style injection. The noise branch contributes three additive perturbations (z₁⊗ψ₁, z₂⊗ψ₂, z₃⊗ψ₃) from thin 4×4×1 or 8×8×1 noise volumes, each scaled and broadcast across all channels to introduce stochastic spatial variation at different resolutions. Underbrace labels at the bottom group the three columns under the headings Main generative pipeline, Noise, and Style. This figure demonstrates how StyleGAN separates high-level content from fine-grained stochastic detail by injecting global style information through adaptive normalization and local noise directly into the feature maps at each scale.

interactions.label: Trace StyleGAN data flow
interactions.teaches: The learner sees that latent z is first mapped to w, w feeds separate per-layer style transforms, and each resulting style vector modulates the synthesis features at its own resolution before the final image is produced

interactions.label: Noise scale ψ
interactions.teaches: The learner sees that the noise maps are spatial single-channel perturbations whose scaled values are broadcast across all 512 channels at the matching resolution, adding stochastic detail without changing the global style path

demo_steps.title: Default StyleGAN flow
demo_steps.narration: With ψ=1, play the trace to follow z through the mapping network into w, then into the three style vectors y1, y2, and y3. Each style vector reaches a different synthesis block and applies per-channel scale and offset at that resolution.

demo_steps.title: Turn off stochastic noise
demo_steps.narration: Set ψ=0 so the top noise slabs and their downward arrows fade out. The style path still modulates the synthesis blocks, showing that style control and stochastic noise are separate inputs.

demo_steps.title: Increase local variation
demo_steps.narration: Raise ψ to a large value so the noise arrows thicken and all 512 channels at each affected block are highlighted. The same one-channel spatial noise pattern is broadcast through the channel dimension at each resolution.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use an oblique diagram layout matching the source: front faces are true horizontal/vertical rectangles in X-Y, and +Z is the receding diagonal drawn up and to the right. Overall world-space canvas about X=0 to 16, Y=-4.8 to 4.8, Z=0 to 1.2. Left curly braces are flat black 2D curves at X≈0.7: Noise band spans Y≈2.3 to 4.8, Main generative pipeline spans Y≈-0.7 to 2.0, Style band spans Y≈-4.5 to -2.0. Text labels sit to the left of each brace. Main pipeline sits around Y=0: learned constant feature cuboid at X≈3.5, dimensions 2.0 × 0.9 × 0.35, light gray #c7d0d2 with dark gray side #4b5658, label above '4×4×512'. First insertion pair centered near X≈5.65: two thin rounded vertical slabs, each about 0.28 × 0.8 × 0.10, light cyan #9bdad2 then dark blue #496d7f. First orange synthesis cuboid at X≈6.5, dimensions 2.25 × 0.9 × 0.85, orange front #d58260, dark brown side #7b3f25, label above '4×4×512'. Second insertion pair centered near X≈8.65 with the same dimensions and colors. Second orange synthesis cuboid at X≈9.55, dimensions 2.3 × 1.45 × 0.9, label above '8×8×512'. Third insertion pair centered near X≈11.95, dimensions 0.34 × 1.45 × 0.12 each, light cyan then dark blue. Third orange synthesis cuboid at X≈12.95, dimensions 2.35 × 1.45 × 0.9, label above '8×8×512'. Final image plane at X≈15.25, dimensions about 0.55 × 1.65 × 0.08, vertical, with black outline and a brown/tan checker texture using #3a160c, #7c3f20, #c88b52, #e0b878. Noise slabs above: z1 at X≈5.65,Y≈3.0 dimensions 0.35 × 0.8 × 0.06, z2 at X≈8.65,Y≈3.0 same size, z3 at X≈11.85,Y≈3.15 dimensions 0.65 × 1.6 × 0.06; all light cyan #9bdad2 with black outline and slight oblique depth. Noise labels are directly above each slab: '4×4×1 Noise z1 ⊗ ψ1', '4×4×1 Noise z2 ⊗ ψ2', and '8×8×1 Noise z3 ⊗ ψ3'. Downward noise arrows are pale blue-gray #b7cbd5 from each noise slab to the corresponding cyan insertion slab. Style branch bottom: latent z cuboid at X≈2.2,Y≈-3.6 dimensions 1.8 × 0.22 × 0.18, light blue-gray #b7cbd5, labeled below '1×1×512' and 'Latent variable z'. Intermediate w cuboid at X≈4.0,Y≈-3.6 dimensions 1.8 × 0.22 × 0.18, orange #d58260, labeled below '1×1×512' and 'Intermediate variable w'. Short arrow from z to w points up-right and is labeled 'Fully connected network'. A dark blue-gray style bus line #4a6878 runs horizontally from just right of w at Y≈-3.45 to X≈11.95, then vertical arrows rise to the three linear transforms. Linear transform cuboids at X≈5.75, 8.65, 11.65 and Y≈-2.45, each dimensions 1.75 × 0.28 × 0.18, orange #d58260, labeled below 'Linear transform' and '2×1×512', with 'Style, y1/y2/y3' above. Upward style arrows continue from each style label to the corresponding insertion pair; the first is annotated 'Per-channel scale and offset'. Channel count 512 should be represented by the equal oblique depth of the 512-channel feature cuboids; 4×4 and 8×8 should be represented by the larger front-face height/width of 8×8 blocks and z3 noise slab. Noise formula for the slider: at layer i, add ψ · ψ_i · z_i[u,v] to every channel c of the feature map at the matching spatial coordinate, i.e. feature_i[u,v,c] += ψ ψ_i z_i[u,v].
interactionPlan.notes: Render cuboids with flat shaded front, top, and side faces plus black outlines to match the textbook diagram. Use CSS2D or bitmap text labels in a serif font similar to the source. Keep the default view fixed and front-facing oblique rather than free orbit. The pipelineTrace animation should create a glowing pulse traveling from latent z to w, splitting along the style bus to the three linear transforms, then moving upward to y1/y2/y3 insertion points; as each insertion point is reached, briefly highlight the corresponding cyan/dark-blue slabs and the adjacent synthesis cuboid. After the third block, pulse into the final checker image. The noiseScale slider should scale noise slab opacity, downward arrow thickness, and a subtle jitter/stripe overlay on the highlighted 512-channel depth faces; at ψ=0 hide or desaturate these noise effects while keeping the geometry and labels visible. Highlight all channels by tinting the oblique side/depth face of the affected synthesis block rather than just a single front slice.

discrepancies: The cyan and dark-blue rounded style/noise injection slabs between synthesis blocks are missing or barely visible, although they are prominent repeated elements in the source.
The top noise maps are rendered as upright rectangular cuboids rather than the slanted parallelogram sheets shown in the reference.
Many labels are crowded and overlap visually, especially the bottom style labels and the z1/z2 noise labels, reducing readability compared with the clean source layout.
The left braces and section labels are too close together and partially intersect visually, unlike the clear grouped brackets in the source.
The overall horizontal spacing is compressed, making the pipeline look more cluttered and less like the wide textbook diagram.
evaluation.notes: The main StyleGAN pipeline structure and colors are recognizable, but missing injection slabs and severe label crowding make it a weaker match to the source.
action_items: Ensure the cyan and dark-blue insertion slabs remain attached to the scene instead of being reparented into an unadded group.
Increase horizontal spacing between pipeline stages so labels and arrows match the open layout of the reference.
Reduce or reposition the bottom style labels and noise labels to prevent overlap and restore the source's clean text hierarchy.
Render the top noise tensors as slanted parallelogram-like sheets rather than front-facing rectangles.

feedback.rationale: The core StyleGAN pipeline concept and interactivity are correct, while the issues are implementation-level rendering, spacing, label, and geometry fixes for the generator.

interactions.label: Trace StyleGAN data flow
interactions.teaches: The learner sees that latent z is first mapped to w, w feeds separate per-layer style transforms, and each resulting style vector modulates the synthesis features at its own resolution before the final image is produced

interactions.label: Noise scale ψ
interactions.teaches: The learner sees that the noise maps are spatial single-channel perturbations whose scaled values are broadcast across all 512 channels at the matching resolution, adding stochastic detail without changing the global style path

demo_steps.title: Default StyleGAN flow
demo_steps.narration: With ψ=1, play the trace to follow z through the mapping network into w, then into the three style vectors y1, y2, and y3. Each style vector reaches a different synthesis block and applies per-channel scale and offset at that resolution.

demo_steps.title: Turn off stochastic noise
demo_steps.narration: Set ψ=0 so the top noise slabs and their downward arrows fade out. The style path still modulates the synthesis blocks, showing that style control and stochastic noise are separate inputs.

demo_steps.title: Increase local variation
demo_steps.narration: Raise ψ to a large value so the noise arrows thicken and all 512 channels at each affected block are highlighted. The same one-channel spatial noise pattern is broadcast through the channel dimension at each resolution.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure illustrates the StyleGAN architecture, organized into three labeled vertical columns: the main generative pipeline (center), the noise injection branch (left of center), and the style branch (right). In the style branch, a latent variable z (1×1×512) is passed through a fully connected network to produce an intermediate variable w (1×1×512), which then feeds three separate linear transforms (each outputting 2×1×512) to generate style vectors y₁, y₂, y₃ that apply per-channel scale and offset adjustments at successive resolution levels of the generator. The main generative pipeline begins with a learned constant input (4×4×512) and passes through convolutional blocks that double in spatial resolution from 4×4×512 to 8×8×512, with each block receiving the corresponding style injection. The noise branch contributes three additive perturbations (z₁⊗ψ₁, z₂⊗ψ₂, z₃⊗ψ₃) from thin 4×4×1 or 8×8×1 noise volumes, each scaled and broadcast across all channels to introduce stochastic spatial variation at different resolutions. Underbrace labels at the bottom group the three columns under the headings Main generative pipeline, Noise, and Style. This figure demonstrates how StyleGAN separates high-level content from fine-grained stochastic detail by injecting global style information through adaptive normalization and local noise directly into the feature maps at each scale.
